u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Yesterday my brother ________ his bike to the park.
u0.explanation: 'Yesterday' tells us it happened in the past, so we use the simple past tense. The past tense of ride is rode.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Last night we ________ at home because it was raining.
u0.explanation: We use 'were' with we, you and they in the past. 'Was' goes with I, he, she and it.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Amy ________ her homework last night. She forgot!
u0.explanation: Negatives in the past: didn't + the base verb. So we say 'didn't do', never 'didn't did'.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

________ you visit your grandma last Sunday?
u0.explanation: Questions in the past use Did + subject + base verb: Did you visit…?

u0.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

The baby ________ (cry) all night, so Mum was very tired.

mark_scheme: cried (spelling must be correct: consonant + y → change y to i and add -ed)

u0.explanation: 'Cry' ends in consonant + y, so change y to i and add -ed: cried.

u0.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

Two days ago, Ken ________ (stop) at the shop and bought some bread.

mark_scheme: stopped (double the p before -ed)

u0.explanation: 'Stop' has one vowel and one consonant at the end, so we double the p: stopped.

u0.stem:
Make a question for the word(s) in [square brackets].

They went to [Ocean Park] last Saturday.

mark_scheme: Where did they go last Saturday? (accept 'Where did they go?'; must use did + base verb 'go', not 'went'; question mark needed)

u0.explanation: We ask about a place with 'Where'. In the past we use did + base verb: Where did they go last Saturday?

u0.stem:
Read Ka Yan's diary and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given verbs.

Last Sunday, I (1) ________ (go) to the beach with my cousins. We (2) ________ (swim) in the sea and (3) ________ (build) a big sandcastle. At noon, we (4) ________ (have) a picnic under a tree. We (5) ________ (not see) any jellyfish, luckily!

mark_scheme: Answer: went
Answer: swam
Answer: built
Answer: had
Answer: didn't see / did not see

u0.explanation: A diary tells about the past, so every verb is in the simple past tense. Go, swim, build and have are irregular: went, swam, built, had. The negative is didn't + base verb: didn't see.

u0.stem: There is one mistake in each line. Find the mistake and write the correct word.

parts.prompt: Yesterday I go to the library with Tom.
mark_scheme: Answer: went (the mistake is 'go'). Accept the correct word alone, or 'go → went'. Spelling and capital letters must be correct.

parts.prompt: We readed some comic books there.
mark_scheme: Answer: read (the mistake is 'readed'). Accept the correct word alone, or 'readed → read'. Spelling and capital letters must be correct.

parts.prompt: Did you saw my new schoolbag?
mark_scheme: Answer: see (the mistake is 'saw'). Accept the correct word alone, or 'saw → see'. Spelling and capital letters must be correct.
Answer: were (the mistake is 'was'). Accept the correct word alone, or 'was → were'. Spelling and capital letters must be correct.

u0.explanation: Line 1: 'Yesterday' needs the past: went. Line 2: read is irregular; its past is read (said 'red'). Line 3: after Did, use the base verb: see. Line 4: 'books' is plural, so use were.

u0.stem:
Read the text from 'A day at Tai O'.

In the afternoon, they took a small boat. "Look! A dolphin!" shouted Ka Ho, but it was only a big wave. Everyone laughed.

Why did everyone laugh?
options: Ka Ho thought a big wave was a dolphin.
Ka Ho fell into the sea.
u0.explanation: Ka Ho shouted 'Look! A dolphin!' but it was only a big wave, so everyone laughed.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We ________ football after school yesterday.
u0.explanation: 'Yesterday' means the past. Regular verbs add -ed: played.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Mum ________ a cake for my birthday last week.
u0.explanation: Make is irregular. Its past tense is made.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I ________ very tired after the swimming lesson.
u0.explanation: Use 'was' with I, he, she and it in the past.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which word is the past tense of 'eat'?
u0.explanation: Eat is irregular: eat → ate.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My cousins ________ to Hong Kong last summer.
u0.explanation: Last summer is in the past. Come → came.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

________ Tom finish his homework last night?
u0.explanation: Past questions start with Did + base verb: Did Tom finish …?

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We didn't ________ the film because the cinema was full.
u0.explanation: After didn't we always use the base verb: didn't see.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence is correct?
options: She did bought a new bag.
She buys a new bag yesterday.
u0.explanation: Buy is irregular: bought. 'Buyed' is not a word.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

The children ________ in the park when it started to rain.
u0.explanation: The children = they, so use 'were' in the past.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Read: 'Ben goes to the library every Saturday. Last Saturday he ________ there with his sister.'
u0.explanation: The first sentence is a habit (present), but 'last Saturday' is one time in the past, so we need went.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Find the mistake: 'Last Monday I wake up late, so I missed the school bus.'
u0.explanation: The story is in the past, so 'wake' should be 'woke'. 'Missed' is already past.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Ka Ho says: 'I didn't went to the party.' How should he say it?
options: I don't went to the party.
I not went to the party.
I didn't gone to the party.
I didn't go to the party.
u0.explanation: didn't + base verb: didn't go.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which question asks about a finished event in the past?
options: Will you go to the beach?
Did you enjoy the beach trip?
Are you going to the beach?
u0.explanation: Did + base verb asks about something already finished.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Choose the word that makes this sentence true: 'There ________ two birthday cakes at the party yesterday.'
u0.explanation: Two cakes is plural and it was yesterday, so we use were.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Read: 'Amy was at home all day on Sunday. She read a book and watched TV.' Which sentence must be TRUE?
options: Amy is reading a book now.
Amy stayed at home on Sunday.
Amy went to the park on Sunday.
u0.explanation: She was at home all day, so she stayed at home. The other sentences go against the text or talk about now.

u0.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence uses the past tense correctly in every verb?
options: We goed to the zoo and saw a lion.
We went to the zoo and see a lion.
We go to the zoo and saw a lion.
We went to the zoo and saw a lion.
u0.explanation: Both actions are in the past: went and saw. Mixing tenses is a common mistake.

u0.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

We ________ (stop) at a shop to buy some drinks.

mark_scheme: stopped (double the p before -ed)

u0.explanation: Short verbs ending consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped.

u0.stem:
Rewrite the sentence as a negative.

Peter caught the bus this morning.

mark_scheme: Peter didn't catch the bus this morning. / Peter did not catch the bus this morning.

u0.explanation: Negative past: didn't + base verb, so caught becomes catch.

u0.stem:
Make a question for the answer.

Answer: Yes, I visited my grandma last Sunday.
Question: ________?

mark_scheme: Did you visit your grandma last Sunday?

u0.explanation: Past question: Did + you + base verb (visit) …?

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My sister ________ the piano every Sunday.
u1.explanation: 'Every Sunday' is a habit, so we use the simple present. With he/she/it we add -s: plays.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look! The children ________ in the rain.
u1.explanation: 'Look!' tells us it is happening now, so we use the present continuous. 'The children' is plural: are dancing.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Tom ________ eat vegetables. He doesn't like them.
u1.explanation: With he/she/it, the negative is doesn't + base verb: Tom doesn't eat vegetables.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence is correct?
u1.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go after am/is/are: She is always happy.

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

My dad ________ (watch) the news every evening.

mark_scheme: watches (add -es after ch)

u1.explanation: 'Every evening' is a habit. Verbs ending in ch add -es with he/she/it: watches.

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

Be quiet! The baby ________ (sleep) now.

mark_scheme: is sleeping

u1.explanation: 'Now' tells us it is happening at the moment: is + verb-ing = is sleeping.

u1.stem:
Rewrite the sentence using the word in brackets.

I go swimming on Saturdays. (usually)

mark_scheme: I usually go swimming on Saturdays. (usually must come before 'go')

u1.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: I usually go swimming on Saturdays.

u1.stem:
Read Mei's message and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given verbs.

Hi Grandma! It's Sunday morning. Right now, I (1) ________ (sit) in the living room. Dad (2) ________ (cook) breakfast in the kitchen. On weekdays, he (3) ________ (go) to work at seven o'clock, so he (4) ________ (not cook) breakfast. My brother never (5) ________ (get) up early!

mark_scheme: Answer: am sitting
Answer: is cooking
Answer: goes
Answer: doesn't cook / does not cook
Answer: gets

u1.explanation: (1) and (2) happen 'right now', so they use am/is + -ing (sitting doubles the t). (3)–(5) are habits on weekdays, so they use the simple present: goes, doesn't cook, gets.

u1.stem:
Read the text from 'Leo's school day'.

Today is different. It is Saturday, and Leo is not at school. Right now, he is sitting in the living room. He is helping his grandfather to fix an old radio.

What is Leo doing right now?
options: He is taking the school bus.
He is helping his grandfather fix a radio.
u1.explanation: The passage says: 'Right now, he is sitting in the living room. He is helping his grandfather to fix an old radio.'

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My dad ________ to work by MTR every day.
u1.explanation: Every day is a habit, and with he/she/it we add -es: goes.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look! The baby ________.
u1.explanation: 'Look!' means it's happening now, so use the present continuous: is sleeping.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

They ________ English on Mondays and Wednesdays.
u1.explanation: They + have. On Mondays is a habit.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which word is spelt correctly?
u1.explanation: Run ends consonant-vowel-consonant, so double the n: running.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Mary ________ her teeth twice a day.
u1.explanation: Verbs ending in -sh add -es: brushes. Twice a day is a habit.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Be quiet! Grandpa ________ the news.
u1.explanation: Be quiet! tells us it is happening right now.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

________ your sister like durian?
u1.explanation: Your sister = she, so the question uses Does.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I ________ my homework now. I'll call you later.
u1.explanation: Now → present continuous: am doing.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Tom ________ eat meat. He is a vegetarian.
u1.explanation: He/she/it + doesn't + base verb.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Find the mistake: 'Every morning, Lily is drinking a glass of milk.'
u1.explanation: Every morning is a habit, so it should be 'drinks'.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence talks about something happening right now?
options: The children are flying kites in the park.
The sun rises in the east.
My mum works in a hospital.
u1.explanation: Are flying (present continuous) shows an action happening now. The others are facts or habits.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Choose the best pair: 'Usually Ken ________ to school, but today he ________ the bus because it's raining.'
u1.explanation: Usually = habit (walks). Today, something different = happening now (is taking).

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which question is correct?
u1.explanation: Does + base verb: Does she like …? The -s goes on does, not on like.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Read: 'Sam is wearing a coat and gloves. He is holding a hot drink.' What is the weather most likely to be?
u1.explanation: A coat, gloves and a hot drink all suggest it is cold.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence is a fact that is always true?
options: Water is boiling in the kettle.
u1.explanation: Facts that are always true use the simple present: boils.

u1.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Mia says: 'I am knowing the answer.' What is wrong?
options: 'Know' is not usually used in the -ing form.
u1.explanation: Verbs like know, like and want describe states, not actions, so we say 'I know the answer.'

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

My brother ________ (study) in his room at the moment.

mark_scheme: is studying

u1.explanation: At the moment → present continuous: is studying.

u1.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given verb.

She ________ (fly) to Taipei every summer.

mark_scheme: flies (y → ies)

u1.explanation: Every summer is a habit. Fly ends consonant + y, so change y to ies: flies.

u1.stem:
Correct the mistake in this sentence and write the correct sentence.

My cat sleep on the sofa every afternoon.

mark_scheme: My cat sleeps on the sofa every afternoon.

u1.explanation: My cat = it, so the verb needs -s: sleeps.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look at those dark clouds! It ________ rain.
u2.explanation: We can see the clouds, so we know it is coming: is going to + base verb.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

"I'm thirsty." "I ________ get you a glass of water."
u2.explanation: This is an offer decided right now, so we use will: I will (I'll) get you a glass of water.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We ________ visit our cousins in Macau next weekend. We bought the ferry tickets yesterday.
u2.explanation: It is a plan made before (they bought tickets), so we use going to. 'We' goes with are: are going to.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I think the test ________ easy tomorrow.
u2.explanation: 'I think' + a guess about the future → will + base verb: will be.

u2.stem:
Fill in the blank with the negative form of 'be going to'.

She ________ join the dance club this year. She is too busy.

mark_scheme: isn't going to / is not going to

u2.explanation: Negative of going to: is not (isn't) going to + base verb.

u2.stem:
Make a question for the word(s) in [square brackets].

They are going to have a party [next Friday].

mark_scheme: When are they going to have a party? (accept 'When are they going to have the party?')

u2.explanation: We ask about time with 'When'. Move 'are' before 'they': When are they going to have a party?

u2.stem:
Read the email and fill in the blanks with 'will' or the correct form of 'be going to'.

Hi Sam,
Next Saturday, my family (1) ________ (visit) the Science Museum. We planned it last week. My sister (2) ________ (bring) her camera. I think it (3) ________ (be) very interesting. Can you come too? I (4) ________ (ask) my mum to buy a ticket for you!
Luke

mark_scheme: Answer: is going to visit (accept 'are going to visit')
Answer: is going to bring
Answer: will be
Answer: will ask (accept 'I'll ask')

u2.explanation: (1) and (2) are plans made before, so we use going to. In (1), 'my family' can take 'is' or 'are': both are correct. (3) is a guess with 'I think' → will be. (4) is an offer decided now → will ask.

u2.stem:
Read the text from 'Plans for the Christmas holiday'.

"My family is going to visit my grandparents in Guangzhou," says Amy. "We are going to take the high-speed train."

How is Amy going to travel to Guangzhou?
u2.explanation: Amy says: 'We are going to take the high-speed train.'

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Look at those dark clouds. It ________ rain.
u2.explanation: We use 'going to' when we can see something will happen.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I think Hong Kong ________ win the match.
u2.explanation: We use will for what we think or guess about the future.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We ________ to visit Ocean Park next Saturday.
u2.explanation: We + are going to. Next Saturday is a plan.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which word shows the future?
u2.explanation: Tomorrow is in the future.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

'The phone is ringing.' 'I ________ get it!'
u2.explanation: A quick decision made at the moment of speaking uses will.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My sister ________ a doctor when she grows up.
u2.explanation: Is going to + base verb: is going to be.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

________ you help me carry this box, please?
u2.explanation: Will you …? is a polite way to ask for help.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

They ________ not going to buy a new car this year.
u2.explanation: They + are: They are not going to …

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence is correct?
options: I will to call you tonight.
u2.explanation: Will + base verb, with no 'to': will call.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Amy has bought paint and brushes. What will she most likely say?
options: I paint my room every day.
I painted my room last year.
I'm going to paint my room.
u2.explanation: She has already got the things, so it's a plan: I'm going to paint …

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Find the mistake: 'Next week we are go to have a test.'
u2.explanation: It should be 'are going to have'.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which answer is a promise?
options: I will tidy my room after dinner, Mum.
u2.explanation: Promises often use will: I will tidy …

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

'Watch out! You ________ fall off the wall!'
u2.explanation: We can see it is about to happen, so we use 'are going to'.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Read: 'Ken has a ticket for the 3 p.m. ferry to Cheung Chau tomorrow.' Which sentence is TRUE?
options: Ken will buy a ticket tomorrow.
Ken is going to Cheung Chau tomorrow.
Ken went to Cheung Chau yesterday.
u2.explanation: He already has a ticket for tomorrow, so he is going to go then.

u2.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which sentence talks about a guess, not a plan?
options: She's going to visit her aunt.
We're going to move house in June.
I'm going to start piano lessons.
I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
u2.explanation: 'I think … will' is a guess. The others are plans.

u2.stem:
Fill in the blank with 'will' or 'going to'.

I've decided. I ________ join the drama club this year.

mark_scheme: am going to / 'm going to

u2.explanation: A decision made before now is a plan: going to.

u2.stem:
Rewrite the sentence as a question.

They are going to watch the fireworks.

mark_scheme: Are they going to watch the fireworks?

u2.explanation: Move 'are' to the front to make a question.

u2.stem: Write one sentence about your plan for next weekend using 'going to'.

mark_scheme: Any correct sentence with be + going to + base verb, e.g. I am going to visit my cousins next weekend.

u2.explanation: Be (am/is/are) + going to + base verb.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

An elephant is ________ than a horse.
u3.explanation: We compare two animals, so we use the comparative. 'Big' doubles the g: bigger than.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Tai Mo Shan is ________ mountain in Hong Kong.
u3.explanation: We compare it with all the mountains in Hong Kong, so we use the superlative: the highest.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

This storybook is ________ than that one.
u3.explanation: 'Interesting' is a long adjective, so we use more + adjective + than.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My pencil case is the same ________ yours.
u3.explanation: We say 'the same as'. (We say 'different from'.)

u3.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given adjective.

Today is ________ (hot) day of the year!

mark_scheme: the hottest (double the t)

u3.explanation: One day compared with all the days of the year → superlative. 'Hot' doubles the t: the hottest.

u3.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the given adjective.

My handwriting is bad, but my brother's handwriting is ________ (bad).

mark_scheme: worse

u3.explanation: 'Bad' is irregular: bad → worse → the worst.

u3.stem:
Rewrite the sentence using 'as … as'.

Peter is 140 cm tall. Paul is 140 cm tall too.

mark_scheme: Peter is as tall as Paul. (accept 'Paul is as tall as Peter.')

u3.explanation: When two things are the same, we use as + adjective + as: Peter is as tall as Paul.

u3.stem:
Look at the information and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the given adjectives.

Pets in the shop: Hamster $80, 10 cm · Rabbit $300, 40 cm · Puppy $5,000, 50 cm

The hamster is (1) ________ (cheap) pet. The rabbit is (2) ________ (big) than the hamster. The puppy is (3) ________ (expensive) pet in the shop. The rabbit is (4) ________ (small) than the puppy.

mark_scheme: Answer: the cheapest
Answer: bigger
Answer: the most expensive
Answer: smaller

u3.explanation: (1) and (3) compare one pet with all the pets → the cheapest, the most expensive. (2) and (4) compare two pets → bigger, smaller + than.

u3.stem:
Read the text from 'Choosing a pet'.

Last, they see a puppy. It is the cutest animal in the shop, but it is also the most expensive. "A puppy needs more space than a rabbit," says Dad. "Our flat isn't as big as Grandma's house." In the end, Mia chooses the rabbit.

Why did Mia's family NOT choose the puppy?
options: It needs more space and their flat is small.
u3.explanation: Dad says a puppy needs more space than a rabbit, and their flat isn't as big as Grandma's house.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

An elephant is ________ than a dog.
u3.explanation: Comparing two things: bigger than. Double the g.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Mount Everest is the ________ mountain in the world.
u3.explanation: The … in the world = superlative: the highest.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My bag is ________ than yours.
u3.explanation: Heavy ends in y, so change y to i: heavier.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

This is the ________ day of my life!
u3.explanation: Good → better → best.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Maths is ________ than art for me.
u3.explanation: Long words use more: more difficult than.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Lily is the ________ girl in our class.
u3.explanation: Short word, superlative: the tallest.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Today is ________ than yesterday. It's 35°C!
u3.explanation: Hot → hotter (double the t).

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

My handwriting is ________ than my brother's.
u3.explanation: Bad → worse → worst.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which is the correct sentence?
options: A car is more fast than a bike.
A car is fast than a bike.
A car is fastest than a bike.
A car is faster than a bike.
u3.explanation: Fast is a short word: faster than.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Tom is 140 cm. Ben is 135 cm. Sam is 150 cm. Who is the shortest?
u3.explanation: 135 cm is the smallest number, so Ben is the shortest.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Find the mistake: 'This is the most beautifullest park in Hong Kong.'
u3.explanation: Use 'most beautiful', not both most and -est.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

A pen costs $8. A ruler costs $5. A book costs $40. Which sentence is TRUE?
options: The pen is more expensive than the book.
The ruler is the most expensive.
The book is the most expensive.
The pen is cheaper than the ruler.
u3.explanation: $40 is the highest price, so the book is the most expensive.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

'My room is ________ than yours, so let's play in mine.'
u3.explanation: Comparing two rooms: bigger than.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Read: 'The red team scored 12 points, the blue team scored 15 and the green team scored 9.' Which sentence is NOT true?
options: Green scored fewer points than red.
Red scored more points than blue.
u3.explanation: Red (12) scored fewer than blue (15), so 'Red scored more than blue' is not true.

u3.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Which word completes both sentences? 'Gold is ___ expensive than silver.' and 'This is the ___ interesting book.'
u3.explanation: Comparing two: more expensive than. The top one: the most interesting.

u3.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the word in brackets.

A cheetah is the ________ (fast) land animal.

mark_scheme: fastest

u3.explanation: The … animal = superlative: fastest.

u3.stem:
Fill in the blank with the correct form of the word in brackets.

This question is ________ (easy) than the last one.

mark_scheme: easier (y → ier)

u3.explanation: Easy ends consonant + y: easier.

u3.stem: Write one sentence comparing two of your friends, using a comparative.

mark_scheme: Any correct comparative sentence, e.g. Ann is taller than Kit. / Ben is more careful than Joe.

u3.explanation: Comparative + than: taller than, more careful than.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

How ________ apples are there in the bag?
u4.explanation: Apples can be counted, so we use 'How many'.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

There isn't ________ milk in the fridge.
u4.explanation: In negative sentences we use 'any'. Milk is uncountable, so 'many' and 'a few' are wrong.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

Please add ________ sugar to my tea. Not too much!
u4.explanation: Sugar is uncountable, and we want a small amount, so we use 'a little'.

u4.stem:
Choose the best answer.

There are ________ people on the bus. I can't find a seat!
u4.explanation: People can be counted, and there are more than we want: too many.

Choose the best answer.

I'd like a ________ of orange juice.

Choose the best answer.

We have only a ________ eggs left. Let's buy more.

'Is there ________ sugar in the jar?' 'Yes, there's a little.'

My birthday is ________ May.

Choose the best answer.

The cat is sleeping ________ the table. I can't see it from the top!

Choose the best answer.

The school picnic is ________ Friday morning.

We usually have dinner ________ seven o'clock.

It is cold ________ the morning but warm ________ noon.

On King Street, from left to right: Bank, Bakery, Library. Across the road from the Library: Swimming Pool.

Choose the best answer.

School starts ________ 8 o'clock.

Choose the best answer.

We go swimming ________ Sundays.

Choose the best answer.

The bank is ________ the bakery and the post office.
u5.explanation: Between two things: between the bakery and the post office.

u5.stem:
Choose the best answer.

I'll see you ________ Christmas Day.
u5.explanation: A particular day takes on: on Christmas Day.

u5.stem:
Choose the best answer.

The children are sitting ________ the teacher, so they can see the board.

u5.stem:
Choose the best answer.

We have lunch ________ noon.
u5.explanation: Use at with noon, night and midnight.

Choose the best answer.

My grandparents live ________ Tuen Mun.
u5.explanation: Use in with towns, cities and districts.

Choose the best answer.

Choose the best answer.

Read: 'Lily sits behind Tom. Tom sits behind Ann.' Who sits at the front?

Choose the best answer.

u7.explanation: Then shows the next step.
